text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Government panel recommends El Al fly on Jewish sabbath.
- Foreign Minister David Levy: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu made new proposals at summit with Egypt.
- 250 million shekels spent on settlers' security since 1994.
- Bank Leumi generates 1.15 billion shekels in largest-ever Tel Aviv Stock Exchange offering. Government expects to raise three billion shekels from bank sales this year.
- Clal first-quarter net income down 66 percent.
- Manufacturers Association head: Netanyahu about to decide on economic policy in face of deteriorating situation.
- Netanyahu proposal for final-status accord: About 40 percent of the West Bank goes to the Palestinians.
- Israeli army position: At least 40 percent of the West Bank territories in Israeli hands.
- 23 professors: "Netanyahu doesn't deserve honour of Hebrew University."
- Intelligence officials expect change in Iranian foreign policy.
